e-5533.knowledge_point: Finding a Block Diagonalization of a 3x3 Matrix
e-5533.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071697/assets/7014ce766be779f4231c78a99a6e013bfc48bfd9e21da7fa565c49e466437c99.png)
Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. Find a block diagonal matrix $B,$ where the $2 \times 2$ block represents a rotation-scaling matrix, such that $A=PBP^{-1}.$
e-5533.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\color{red}\lambda_1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${\color{red}{\mathbf{v}_1}},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\color{blue}\lambda_2} = \overline{\color{blue}\lambda}_{\color{blue}3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${\color{blue}\mathbf{v}_2} = \overline{\color{blue}\mathbf{v}}_{\color{blue}3},$ then $A=PBP^{-1},$ where
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071697/assets/5e03c481312af462a0739b4670e24325d2e06cc10449c65bfb04208206fc5d58.png)
Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

To compute the eigenvalues of $A,$ we solve the characteristic equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-2-\lambda  & 0 & 1 \\ 3 & -1-\lambda  & 5 \\ -1 & 0 & -2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )((-2-\lambda )^{2}-1(-1)) & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+4\lambda +5) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the real eigenvalue is 
$\lambda_1={\color{red}-1}.$
Now, using the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{2,3} & =\frac{-4\pm \sqrt{(4)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 5}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-4\pm \sqrt{-4}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-4\pm 2\text{i}}{2} \\  & =-2\pm \text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the block diagonal matrix is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071697/assets/712c3f663a367090ab5ba81705e7c7f36ce6d4e2d6e2b13cc59383421e408ea7.png)

Question 1
?

P=[54−3−23−1012],B=[340−430002]

Consider the nonsingular matrix P and the block diagonal matrix B shown above, where the 2×2 block of B is a rotation-scaling matrix. Given that A=PBP−1, what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of A?

a
λ=3±4i and v=[5±4i−2±3i±i]
b
λ=4±3i and v=[−5±4i2±3i±i]
c
λ=3±2i and v=[5±4i2∓3i2±i]
d
λ=−3±4i and v=[∓4i−2±3i±i]
e
λ=−2±3i and v=[5±4i2±3i∓i]
Submit

decision.explanation: The 2×2 block has eigenvalues 3±4i with eigenvectors (1,±i,0)^T. Since A=PBP^{-1}, multiplying these vectors by P gives (5±4i,-2±3i,±i)^T, with matching signs. Thus option a is correct.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}5 & 4 & -3 \\ -2 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 & 0 \\ -4 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the nonsingular matrix $P$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown above, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ is a rotation-scaling matrix.
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $3\times 3$ real matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

- From our block diagonal matrix 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 & 0 \\ -4 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce the complex eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1,2}=3\pm 4\text{i}$ and the real eigenvalue is ${\lambda }_{3}=2.$

- From our matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}5 & 4 & -3 \\ -2 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the complex and real eigenvectors are

$$
{v}_{1,2}=[\begin{aligned}5\pm 4\text{i} \\ -2\pm 3\text{i} \\ \pm \text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 1
?

P=[54−3−23−1012],B=[340−430002]

Consider the nonsingular matrix P and the block diagonal matrix B shown above, where the 2×2 block of B is a rotation-scaling matrix. Given that A=PBP−1, what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of A?

a
λ=3±4i and v=[5±4i−2±3i±i]
b
λ=4±3i and v=[−5±4i2±3i±i]
c
λ=3±2i and v=[5±4i2∓3i2±i]
d
λ=−3±4i and v=[∓4i−2±3i±i]
e
λ=−2±3i and v=[5±4i2±3i∓i]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a 3×3 real matrix that has one real eigenvalue λ1 with corresponding eigenvector v1, and two complex eigenvalues λ2=λ―3 with corresponding eigenvectors v2=v―3, then A=PBP−1, where B=[λ1000Re(λ2)Im(λ2)0−Im(λ2)Re(λ2)],P=[|||v1Re(v2)Im(v2)|||]. Notice that swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

  • From our block diagonal matrix B=[340−430002], we deduce the complex eigenvalues are λ1,2=3±4i and the real eigenvalue is λ3=2.

  • From our matrix P=[54−3−23−1012], we deduce that the complex and real eigenvectors are v1,2=[5±4i−2±3i±i],v3=[−3−12].

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms option a. Directly, B(1,±i,0)^T=(3±4i)(1,±i,0)^T. Multiplication by P gives the corresponding eigenvectors (5±4i,-2±3i,±i)^T of A=PBP^{-1}.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Eigenvalues and Corresponding Eigenvectors of a Matrix in Block Diagonal Form
content.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}5 & 4 & -3 \\ -2 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 & 0 \\ -4 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the nonsingular matrix $P$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown above, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ is a rotation-scaling matrix.
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $3\times 3$ real matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

- From our block diagonal matrix 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 & 0 \\ -4 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce the complex eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1,2}=3\pm 4\text{i}$ and the real eigenvalue is ${\lambda }_{3}=2.$

- From our matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}5 & 4 & -3 \\ -2 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the complex and real eigenvectors are

$$
{v}_{1,2}=[\begin{aligned}5\pm 4\text{i} \\ -2\pm 3\text{i} \\ \pm \text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the nonsingular matrix $P$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown above, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ is a rotation-scaling matrix.

decision.explanation: The rotation-scaling block has eigenvalues -2±5i and corresponding eigenvectors (0,1,±i)^T of B. Multiplying by P gives its second column ±i times its third column: (-2,∓2i,1∓i)^T. These are corresponding eigenvectors of A, so option b is correct.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & -5 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the nonsingular matrix $P$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown above, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ is a rotation-scaling matrix.
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $3\times 3$ real matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

- From our block diagonal matrix 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & -5 & -2\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce the complex eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{2,3}=-2\pm 5\text{i}$ and the real eigenvalue is ${\lambda }_{1}=-7.$

- From our matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the complex and real eigenvectors are

$$
{v}_{2,3}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ ∓2\text{i} \\ 1∓\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 2
?

P=[1−2050−201−1],B=[−7000−250−5−2]

Consider the nonsingular matrix P and the block diagonal matrix B shown above, where the 2×2 block of B is a rotation-scaling matrix. Given that A=PBP−1, what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of A?

a
λ=5±2i and v=[2i∓2i1∓i]
b
λ=−2±5i and v=[−2∓2i1∓i]
c
λ=1±5i and v=[−2∓2i1∓i]
d
λ=−2±5i and v=[−21±2i∓i]
e
λ=5±2i and v=[−2±2 1∓i]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a 3×3 real matrix that has one real eigenvalue λ1 with corresponding eigenvector v1, and two complex eigenvalues λ2=λ―3 with corresponding eigenvectors v2=v―3, then A=PBP−1, where B=[λ1000Re(λ2)Im(λ2)0−Im(λ2)Re(λ2)],P=[|||v1Re(v2)Im(v2)|||]. Notice that swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

  • From our block diagonal matrix B=[−7000−250−5−2], we deduce the complex eigenvalues are λ2,3=−2±5i and the real eigenvalue is λ1=−7.

  • From our matrix P=[1−2050−201−1], we deduce that the complex and real eigenvectors are v2,3=[−2∓2i1∓i],v1=[150].

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Eigenvalues and Corresponding Eigenvectors of a Matrix in Block Diagonal Form
content.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & -5 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the nonsingular matrix $P$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown above, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ is a rotation-scaling matrix.
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $3\times 3$ real matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

- From our block diagonal matrix 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & -5 & -2\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce the complex eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{2,3}=-2\pm 5\text{i}$ and the real eigenvalue is ${\lambda }_{1}=-7.$

- From our matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the complex and real eigenvectors are

$$
{v}_{2,3}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ ∓2\text{i} \\ 1∓\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 3
?

P=[240−3−1−2054],B=[4000340−43]

Consider the nonsingular matrix P and the block diagonal matrix B shown above, where the 2×2 block of B is a rotation-scaling matrix. Given that A=PBP−1, what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of A?

a
λ=1±4i and v=[4−1±2i−5±4i]
b
λ=−3±4i and v=[11∓2i5±4i]
c
λ=3±i and v=[2−1∓4i5±2i]
d
λ=3±4i and v=[4−1∓2i5±4i]
e
λ=4±3i and v=[−4−1∓2i5∓4i]
Submit

decision.explanation: The 2×2 block of B has eigenvalues 3±4i with eigenvectors (0,1,±i)^T. Multiplying by P gives (4,-1∓2i,5±4i)^T. Since A=PBP^{-1}, these are the corresponding eigenvectors of A, proving option d.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 0 \\ -3 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 5 & 4\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & -4 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the nonsingular matrix $P$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown above, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ is a rotation-scaling matrix.
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $3\times 3$ real matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

- From our block diagonal matrix 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & -4 & 3\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce the complex eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{2,3}=3\pm 4\text{i}$ and the real eigenvalue is ${\lambda }_{1}=4.$

- From our matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 0 \\ -3 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 5 & 4\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the complex and real eigenvectors are

$$
{v}_{2,3}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1∓2\text{i} \\ 5\pm 4\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 3
?

P=[240−3−1−2054],B=[4000340−43]

Consider the nonsingular matrix P and the block diagonal matrix B shown above, where the 2×2 block of B is a rotation-scaling matrix. Given that A=PBP−1, what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of A?

a
λ=1±4i and v=[4−1±2i−5±4i]
b
λ=−3±4i and v=[11∓2i5±4i]
c
λ=3±i and v=[2−1∓4i5±2i]
d
λ=3±4i and v=[4−1∓2i5±4i]
e
λ=4±3i and v=[−4−1∓2i5∓4i]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a 3×3 real matrix that has one real eigenvalue λ1 with corresponding eigenvector v1, and two complex eigenvalues λ2=λ―3 with corresponding eigenvectors v2=v―3, then A=PBP−1, where B=[λ1000Re(λ2)Im(λ2)0−Im(λ2)Re(λ2)],P=[|||v1Re(v2)Im(v2)|||]. Notice that swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

  • From our block diagonal matrix B=[4000340−43], we deduce the complex eigenvalues are λ2,3=3±4i and the real eigenvalue is λ1=4.

  • From our matrix P=[240−3−1−2054], we deduce that the complex and real eigenvectors are v2,3=[4−1∓2i5±4i],v1=[2−30].

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option d. The block has eigenvalues 3±4i, and P(0,1,±i)^T=(4,-1∓2i,5±4i)^T gives the corresponding eigenvectors of A=PBP^{-1}.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Eigenvalues and Corresponding Eigenvectors of a Matrix in Block Diagonal Form
content.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 0 \\ -3 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 5 & 4\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & -4 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the nonsingular matrix $P$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown above, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ is a rotation-scaling matrix.
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $3\times 3$ real matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

- From our block diagonal matrix 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & -4 & 3\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce the complex eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{2,3}=3\pm 4\text{i}$ and the real eigenvalue is ${\lambda }_{1}=4.$

- From our matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 0 \\ -3 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 5 & 4\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the complex and real eigenvectors are

$$
{v}_{2,3}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1∓2\text{i} \\ 5\pm 4\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 4
?

P=[1450−7053−2],B=[830−380005]

Consider the nonsingular matrix P and the block diagonal matrix B shown above, where the 2×2 block of B is a rotation-scaling matrix. Given that A=PBP−1, what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of A?

a
λ=5±3i and v=[−1±4i∓7i5±3i]
b
λ=3±8i and v=[1∓4i∓7i3±5i]
c
λ=8±5i and v=[5±i∓7i5∓3i]
d
λ=8±3i and v=[1±4i∓7i5±3i]
e
λ=−8±3i and v=[1±4i±7i−5±3i]
Submit

decision.explanation: The 2×2 block has eigenvalues 8±3i and corresponding eigenvectors (1,±i,0)^T. Multiplying by P gives (1±4i,∓7i,5±3i)^T, the corresponding eigenvectors of A=PBP^{-1}. Thus option d is correct.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 5 \\ 0 & -7 & 0 \\ 5 & 3 & -2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}8 & 3 & 0 \\ -3 & 8 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the nonsingular matrix $P$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown above, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ is a rotation-scaling matrix.
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $3\times 3$ real matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

- From our block diagonal matrix 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}8 & 3 & 0 \\ -3 & 8 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce the complex eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1,2}=8\pm 3\text{i}$ and the real eigenvalue is ${\lambda }_{3}=5.$

- From our matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 5 \\ 0 & -7 & 0 \\ 5 & 3 & -2\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the complex and real eigenvectors are

$$
{v}_{1,2}=[\begin{aligned}1\pm 4\text{i} \\ ∓7\text{i} \\ 5\pm 3\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}].

Question 4
?

P=[1450−7053−2],B=[830−380005]

Consider the nonsingular matrix P and the block diagonal matrix B shown above, where the 2×2 block of B is a rotation-scaling matrix. Given that A=PBP−1, what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of A?

a
λ=5±3i and v=[−1±4i∓7i5±3i]
b
λ=3±8i and v=[1∓4i∓7i3±5i]
c
λ=8±5i and v=[5±i∓7i5∓3i]
d
λ=8±3i and v=[1±4i∓7i5±3i]
e
λ=−8±3i and v=[1±4i±7i−5±3i]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a 3×3 real matrix that has one real eigenvalue λ1 with corresponding eigenvector v1, and two complex eigenvalues λ2=λ―3 with corresponding eigenvectors v2=v―3, then A=PBP−1, where B=[λ1000Re(λ2)Im(λ2)0−Im(λ2)Re(λ2)],P=[|||v1Re(v2)Im(v2)|||]. Notice that swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

  • From our block diagonal matrix B=[830−380005], we deduce the complex eigenvalues are λ1,2=8±3i and the real eigenvalue is λ3=5.

  • From our matrix P=[1450−7053−2], we deduce that the complex and real eigenvectors are v1,2=[1±4i∓7i5±3i],v3=[50−2].

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Eigenvalues and Corresponding Eigenvectors of a Matrix in Block Diagonal Form
content.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 5 \\ 0 & -7 & 0 \\ 5 & 3 & -2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}8 & 3 & 0 \\ -3 & 8 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the nonsingular matrix $P$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown above, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ is a rotation-scaling matrix.
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $3\times 3$ real matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

- From our block diagonal matrix 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}8 & 3 & 0 \\ -3 & 8 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce the complex eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1,2}=8\pm 3\text{i}$ and the real eigenvalue is ${\lambda }_{3}=5.$

- From our matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 5 \\ 0 & -7 & 0 \\ 5 & 3 & -2\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the complex and real eigenvectors are

$$
{v}_{1,2}=[\begin{aligned}1\pm 4\text{i} \\ ∓7\text{i} \\ 5\pm 3\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 5
?

P=[246−30−2153],B=[−1000570−75]

Consider the nonsingular matrix P and the block diagonal matrix B shown above, where the 2×2 block of B is a rotation-scaling matrix. Given that A=PBP−1, what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of A?

a
λ=−5±i and v=[2±6i∓i3∓5i]
b
λ=5±7i and v=[4±6i∓2i5±3i]
c
λ=−5±7i and v=[−4∓6i∓2i1±5i]
d
λ=7±5i and v=[2±6i±2i3±5i]
e
λ=5±i and v=[−4±6i∓2i5∓3i]
Submit

decision.explanation: The 2×2 block of B has eigenvalues 5±7i with eigenvectors (0,1,±i)^T. Multiplying by P gives (4±6i,∓2i,5±3i)^T, the corresponding eigenvectors of A=PBP^{-1}. Thus option b is correct.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 6 \\ -3 & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & 5 & 3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 7 \\ 0 & -7 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the nonsingular matrix $P$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown above, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ is a rotation-scaling matrix.
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $3\times 3$ real matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

- From our block diagonal matrix 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 7 \\ 0 & -7 & 5\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce the complex eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{2,3}=5\pm 7\text{i}$ and the real eigenvalue is ${\lambda }_{1}=-1.$

- From our matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 6 \\ -3 & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & 5 & 3\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the complex and real eigenvectors are

$$
{v}_{2,3}=[\begin{aligned}4\pm 6\text{i} \\ ∓2\text{i} \\ 5\pm 3\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 5
?

P=[246−30−2153],B=[−1000570−75]

Consider the nonsingular matrix P and the block diagonal matrix B shown above, where the 2×2 block of B is a rotation-scaling matrix. Given that A=PBP−1, what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of A?

a
λ=−5±i and v=[2±6i∓i3∓5i]
b
λ=5±7i and v=[4±6i∓2i5±3i]
c
λ=−5±7i and v=[−4∓6i∓2i1±5i]
d
λ=7±5i and v=[2±6i±2i3±5i]
e
λ=5±i and v=[−4±6i∓2i5∓3i]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a 3×3 real matrix that has one real eigenvalue λ1 with corresponding eigenvector v1, and two complex eigenvalues λ2=λ―3 with corresponding eigenvectors v2=v―3, then A=PBP−1, where B=[λ1000Re(λ2)Im(λ2)0−Im(λ2)Re(λ2)],P=[|||v1Re(v2)Im(v2)|||]. Notice that swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

  • From our block diagonal matrix B=[−1000570−75], we deduce the complex eigenvalues are λ2,3=5±7i and the real eigenvalue is λ1=−1.

  • From our matrix P=[246−30−2153], we deduce that the complex and real eigenvectors are v2,3=[4±6i∓2i5±3i],v1=[2−31].

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Eigenvalues and Corresponding Eigenvectors of a Matrix in Block Diagonal Form
content.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 6 \\ -3 & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & 5 & 3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 7 \\ 0 & -7 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the nonsingular matrix $P$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown above, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ is a rotation-scaling matrix.
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $3\times 3$ real matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

- From our block diagonal matrix 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 7 \\ 0 & -7 & 5\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce the complex eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{2,3}=5\pm 7\text{i}$ and the real eigenvalue is ${\lambda }_{1}=-1.$

- From our matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 6 \\ -3 & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & 5 & 3\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the complex and real eigenvectors are

$$
{v}_{2,3}=[\begin{aligned}4\pm 6\text{i} \\ ∓2\text{i} \\ 5\pm 3\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

A=[−10956−2−10−1] Consider the matrix A shown above. Find a block diagonal matrix B, where the 2×2 block represents a rotation-scaling matrix, such that A=PBP−1.

a
B=[3000−160−6−1]
b
B=[1000−630−3−6]
c
B=[6000−130−3−1]
d

decision.explanation: Expanding det(A−λI) along the second column gives (6−λ)((−1−λ)^2+9). Thus the eigenvalues are 6 and −1±3i. The complex pair yields the rotation-scaling block [[−1,3],[−3,−1]], so option c is valid.

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 9 \\ 5 & 6 & -2 \\ -1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. Find a block diagonal matrix $B,$ where the $2\times 2$ block represents a rotation-scaling matrix, such that $A=PB{P}^{-1}.$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

To compute the eigenvalues of $A,$ we solve the characteristic equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & 0 & 9 \\ 5 & 6-\lambda  & -2 \\ -1 & 0 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (6-\lambda )((-1-\lambda )^{2}-9(-1)) & =0 \\ (6-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+2\lambda +10) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the real eigenvalue is 
${\lambda }_{1}=6.$
Now, using the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{2,3} & =\frac{-2\pm \sqrt{(2)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 10}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-2\pm \sqrt{-36}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-2\pm 6\text{i}}{2} \\  & =-1\pm 3\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the block diagonal matrix is

$$

content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 9 \\ 5 & 6 & -2 \\ -1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. Find a block diagonal matrix $B,$ where the $2\times 2$ block represents a rotation-scaling matrix, such that $A=PB{P}^{-1}.$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

To compute the eigenvalues of $A,$ we solve the characteristic equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & 0 & 9 \\ 5 & 6-\lambda  & -2 \\ -1 & 0 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (6-\lambda )((-1-\lambda )^{2}-9(-1)) & =0 \\ (6-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+2\lambda +10) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the real eigenvalue is 
${\lambda }_{1}=6.$
Now, using the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{2,3} & =\frac{-2\pm \sqrt{(2)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 10}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-2\pm \sqrt{-36}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-2\pm 6\text{i}}{2} \\  & =-1\pm 3\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the block diagonal matrix is

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & -3 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

decision.explanation: Expanding along the second column gives det(A−λI)=(2−λ)((−2−λ)(−4−λ)+5)=(2−λ)((λ+3)^2+4). The eigenvalues are 2 and −3±2i. These distinct eigenvalues give a real block diagonalization with rotation-scaling block [[−3,2],[−2,−3]], as in option b.

after.name: Question 7
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 1 \\ 6 & 2 & -3 \\ -5 & 0 & -4\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. Find a block diagonal matrix $B,$ where the $2\times 2$ block represents a rotation-scaling matrix, such that $A=PB{P}^{-1}.$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

To compute the eigenvalues of $A,$ we solve the characteristic equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-2-\lambda  & 0 & 1 \\ 6 & 2-\lambda  & -3 \\ -5 & 0 & -4-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )((-2-\lambda )(-4-\lambda )-1(-5)) & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+6\lambda +13) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the real eigenvalue is 
${\lambda }_{1}=2.$
Now, using the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{2,3} & =\frac{-6\pm \sqrt{(6)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 13}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-6\pm \sqrt{-16}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-6\pm 4\text{i}}{2} \\  & =-3\pm 2\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the block diagonal matrix is

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Block Diagonalization of a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 1 \\ 6 & 2 & -3 \\ -5 & 0 & -4\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. Find a block diagonal matrix $B,$ where the $2\times 2$ block represents a rotation-scaling matrix, such that $A=PB{P}^{-1}.$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

To compute the eigenvalues of $A,$ we solve the characteristic equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-2-\lambda  & 0 & 1 \\ 6 & 2-\lambda  & -3 \\ -5 & 0 & -4-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )((-2-\lambda )(-4-\lambda )-1(-5)) & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+6\lambda +13) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the real eigenvalue is 
${\lambda }_{1}=2.$
Now, using the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{2,3} & =\frac{-6\pm \sqrt{(6)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 13}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-6\pm \sqrt{-16}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-6\pm 4\text{i}}{2} \\  & =-3\pm 2\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the block diagonal matrix is

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

decision.explanation: Expanding along the second column gives det(A−λI)=(−3−λ)((8−λ)(4−λ)+20)=(−3−λ)((λ−6)^2+16). Thus the eigenvalues are −3 and 6±4i. Their real block diagonal form has scalar block −3 and rotation-scaling block [[6,4],[−4,6]], proving option e.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}8 & 0 & 2 \\ 5 & -3 & -1 \\ -10 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. Find a block diagonal matrix $B,$ where the $2\times 2$ block represents a rotation-scaling matrix, such that $A=PB{P}^{-1}.$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

To compute the eigenvalues of $A,$ we solve the characteristic equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}8-\lambda  & 0 & 2 \\ 5 & -3-\lambda  & -1 \\ -10 & 0 & 4-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-3-\lambda )((8-\lambda )(4-\lambda )-2(-10)) & =0 \\ (-3-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-12\lambda +52) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the real eigenvalue is 
${\lambda }_{1}=-3.$
Now, using the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{2,3} & =\frac{12\pm \sqrt{(-12)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 52}}{2} \\  & =\frac{12\pm \sqrt{-64}}{2} \\  & =\frac{12\pm 8\text{i}}{2} \\  & =6\pm 4\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the block diagonal matrix is

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 6 & 4 \\ 0 & -4 & 6\end{aligned}].
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Block Diagonalization of a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}8 & 0 & 2 \\ 5 & -3 & -1 \\ -10 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. Find a block diagonal matrix $B,$ where the $2\times 2$ block represents a rotation-scaling matrix, such that $A=PB{P}^{-1}.$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

To compute the eigenvalues of $A,$ we solve the characteristic equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}8-\lambda  & 0 & 2 \\ 5 & -3-\lambda  & -1 \\ -10 & 0 & 4-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-3-\lambda )((8-\lambda )(4-\lambda )-2(-10)) & =0 \\ (-3-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-12\lambda +52) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the real eigenvalue is 
${\lambda }_{1}=-3.$
Now, using the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{2,3} & =\frac{12\pm \sqrt{(-12)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 52}}{2} \\  & =\frac{12\pm \sqrt{-64}}{2} \\  & =\frac{12\pm 8\text{i}}{2} \\  & =6\pm 4\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the block diagonal matrix is

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 6 & 4 \\ 0 & -4 & 6\end{aligned}].
$$

A=[−205843−50−2] Consider the matrix A shown above. Find a block diagonal matrix B, where the 2×2 block represents a rotation-scaling matrix, such that A=PBP−1.

a
B=[−4000520−25]
b
B=[2000450−54]
c
B=[4000−230−3−2]
d
B=[4000−260−6−2]
e
B=[4000−250−5−2]
Submit

decision.explanation: Expanding along the second column gives det(A−λI)=(4−λ)((λ+2)^2+25). Hence the eigenvalues are 4 and −2±5i. These distinct eigenvalues give a real block diagonalization with scalar block 4 and rotation-scaling block [[−2,5],[−5,−2]], which is option e.

after.name: Question 9
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 5 \\ 8 & 4 & 3 \\ -5 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. Find a block diagonal matrix $B,$ where the $2\times 2$ block represents a rotation-scaling matrix, such that $A=PB{P}^{-1}.$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

To compute the eigenvalues of $A,$ we solve the characteristic equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-2-\lambda  & 0 & 5 \\ 8 & 4-\lambda  & 3 \\ -5 & 0 & -2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )((-2-\lambda )^{2}-5(-5)) & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+4\lambda +29) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the real eigenvalue is 
${\lambda }_{1}=4.$
Now, using the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{2,3} & =\frac{-4\pm \sqrt{(4)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 29}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-4\pm \sqrt{-100}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-4\pm 10\text{i}}{2} \\  & =-2\pm 5\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the block diagonal matrix is

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & -5 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Block Diagonalization of a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 5 \\ 8 & 4 & 3 \\ -5 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}]

Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. Find a block diagonal matrix $B,$ where the $2\times 2$ block represents a rotation-scaling matrix, such that $A=PB{P}^{-1}.$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

To compute the eigenvalues of $A,$ we solve the characteristic equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-2-\lambda  & 0 & 5 \\ 8 & 4-\lambda  & 3 \\ -5 & 0 & -2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )((-2-\lambda )^{2}-5(-5)) & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+4\lambda +29) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the real eigenvalue is 
${\lambda }_{1}=4.$
Now, using the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{2,3} & =\frac{-4\pm \sqrt{(4)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 29}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-4\pm \sqrt{-100}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-4\pm 10\text{i}}{2} \\  & =-2\pm 5\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the block diagonal matrix is

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & -5 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

decision.explanation: Expanding along the second column gives det(A−λI)=(5−λ)((2−λ)^2+36). The eigenvalues are 5 and 2±6i, so the real block diagonal form has scalar block 5 and rotation-scaling block [[2,6],[−6,2]]. This is option e.

after.name: Question 10
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 4 \\ 1 & 5 & -3 \\ -9 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. Find a block diagonal matrix $B,$ where the $2\times 2$ block represents a rotation-scaling matrix, such that $A=PB{P}^{-1}.$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

To compute the eigenvalues of $A,$ we solve the characteristic equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 0 & 4 \\ 1 & 5-\lambda  & -3 \\ -9 & 0 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (5-\lambda )((2-\lambda )^{2}-4(-9)) & =0 \\ (5-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-4\lambda +40) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the real eigenvalue is 
${\lambda }_{1}=5.$
Now, using the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{2,3} & =\frac{4\pm \sqrt{(-4)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 40}}{2} \\  & =\frac{4\pm \sqrt{-144}}{2} \\  & =\frac{4\pm 12\text{i}}{2} \\  & =2\pm 6\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the block diagonal matrix is

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 6 \\ 0 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Block Diagonalization of a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 4 \\ 1 & 5 & -3 \\ -9 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. Find a block diagonal matrix $B,$ where the $2\times 2$ block represents a rotation-scaling matrix, such that $A=PB{P}^{-1}.$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

To compute the eigenvalues of $A,$ we solve the characteristic equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 0 & 4 \\ 1 & 5-\lambda  & -3 \\ -9 & 0 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (5-\lambda )((2-\lambda )^{2}-4(-9)) & =0 \\ (5-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-4\lambda +40) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the real eigenvalue is 
${\lambda }_{1}=5.$
Now, using the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{2,3} & =\frac{4\pm \sqrt{(-4)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 40}}{2} \\  & =\frac{4\pm \sqrt{-144}}{2} \\  & =\frac{4\pm 12\text{i}}{2} \\  & =2\pm 6\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the block diagonal matrix is

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 6 \\ 0 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3+2\text{i} \\ 4+\text{i} \\ 2+6\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=4-\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=3,$ respectively.

decision.explanation: Since the first block corresponds to 4−i, take the first two columns of P as Re(v₁)=(3,4,2)^T and Im(v₁)=(2,1,6)^T. The third column is v₃=(2,0,3)^T. This gives option b, whose determinant is 29, so P is invertible.

after.name: Question 11
after.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ represents a rotation-scaling matrix:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3+2\text{i} \\ 4+\text{i} \\ 2+6\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=4-\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=3,$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{3},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{2}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{1}={\overset{―}{v}}_{2},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 \\ -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {\lambda }_{3}\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ \text{Re}({v}_{1}) & \text{Im}({v}_{1}) & {v}_{3} \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ will correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the third column of $P$ will correspond to the real eigenvector ${v}_{3}:$

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 2 \\ 4 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 6 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

content.knowledge_point: Calculating the Invertible Matrix in Block Diagonal Form of a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ represents a rotation-scaling matrix:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3+2\text{i} \\ 4+\text{i} \\ 2+6\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=4-\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=3,$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{3},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{2}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{1}={\overset{―}{v}}_{2},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 \\ -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {\lambda }_{3}\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ \text{Re}({v}_{1}) & \text{Im}({v}_{1}) & {v}_{3} \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ will correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the third column of $P$ will correspond to the real eigenvector ${v}_{3}:$

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 2 \\ 4 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 6 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2+5\text{i} \\ 1+3\text{i} \\ 4-7\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 7 \\ 0 & -7 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=5$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=2+7\text{i},$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$

Question 12
?

Consider the vectors v1 and v2 and the block diagonal matrix B shown below, where the 2×2 block of B represents a rotation-scaling matrix: v1=[3−41],v2=[−2+5i1+3i4−7i],B=[5000270−72] The vectors v1 and v2 are the eigenvectors of a matrix A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1=5 and λ2=2+7i, respectively. Given that A=PBP−1, which of the following could be the matrix P?

a
[3−70−13354−2]
b
[3−15−46314−7]
c
[8−25−413−54−7]
d
[3−2621374−1]
e
[3−25−41314−7]
Submit

decision.explanation: Take P=[v₁,Re(v₂),Im(v₂)], matching the scalar block 5 and the complex block for 2+7i. This gives option e. Its determinant is −100, so P is invertible, and P(0,1,i)^T=v₂ verifies the complex eigenvector pairing.

after.name: Question 12
after.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ represents a rotation-scaling matrix:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2+5\text{i} \\ 1+3\text{i} \\ 4-7\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 7 \\ 0 & -7 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=5$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=2+7\text{i},$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 7 \\ 0 & -7 & 2\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first column of $P$ will correspond to the real eigenvector ${v}_{1}$ and the second and third columns of $P$ will correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{2}:$

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 5 \\ -4 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 4 & -7\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the vectors v1 and v2 and the block diagonal matrix B shown below, where the 2×2 block of B represents a rotation-scaling matrix: v1=[3−41],v2=[−2+5i1+3i4−7i],B=[5000270−72] The vectors v1 and v2 are the eigenvectors of a matrix A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1=5 and λ2=2+7i, respectively. Given that A=PBP−1, which of the following could be the matrix P?

a
[3−70−13354−2]
b
[3−15−46314−7]
c
[8−25−413−54−7]
d
[3−2621374−1]
e
[3−25−41314−7]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a real 3×3 matrix that has one real eigenvalue λ1 with corresponding eigenvector v1, and two complex eigenvalues λ2=λ―3 with corresponding eigenvectors v2=v―3, then A=PBP−1, where B=[λ1000Re(λ2)Im(λ2)0−Im(λ2)Re(λ2)],P=[|||v1Re(v2)Im(v2)|||]. Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

From our block diagonal matrix B=[5000270−72], we deduce that the first column of P will correspond to the real eigenvector v1 and the second and third columns of P will correspond to the complex eigenvector v2:

P=[3−25−41314−7]

content.knowledge_point: Calculating the Invertible Matrix in Block Diagonal Form of a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ represents a rotation-scaling matrix:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2+5\text{i} \\ 1+3\text{i} \\ 4-7\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 7 \\ 0 & -7 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=5$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=2+7\text{i},$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 7 \\ 0 & -7 & 2\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first column of $P$ will correspond to the real eigenvector ${v}_{1}$ and the second and third columns of $P$ will correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{2}:$

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 5 \\ -4 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 4 & -7\end{aligned}]
$$

Question 13
?

Consider the vectors v1 and v2 and the block diagonal matrix B shown below, where the 2×2 block of B represents a rotation-scaling matrix: v1=[40−3],v2=[1−i−6+3i−5i],B=[7000480−84] The vectors v1 and v2 are the eigenvectors of a matrix A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1=7 and λ2=4+8i, respectively. Given that A=PBP−1, which of the following could be the matrix P?

a
[21−10−6−3−10−5]
b
[41−10−63−30−5]
c
[412203−32−5]
d
[41−10−36−35−5]
e
[4−10063−302]
Submit

decision.explanation: Use P=[v₁,Re(v₂),Im(v₂)]. Its columns are (4,0,−3)^T, (1,−6,0)^T, and (−1,3,−5)^T, giving option b. Its determinant is 147, so it is invertible; the column arrangement matches the blocks of B.

after.name: Question 13
after.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ represents a rotation-scaling matrix:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} \\ -6+3\text{i} \\ -5\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 8 \\ 0 & -8 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=7$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=4+8\text{i},$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 8 \\ 0 & -8 & 4\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first column of $P$ will correspond to the real eigenvector ${v}_{1}$ and the second and third columns of $P$ will correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{2}:$

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & -6 & 3 \\ -3 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}]
$$

Question 13
?

Consider the vectors v1 and v2 and the block diagonal matrix B shown below, where the 2×2 block of B represents a rotation-scaling matrix: v1=[40−3],v2=[1−i−6+3i−5i],B=[7000480−84] The vectors v1 and v2 are the eigenvectors of a matrix A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1=7 and λ2=4+8i, respectively. Given that A=PBP−1, which of the following could be the matrix P?

a
[21−10−6−3−10−5]
b
[41−10−63−30−5]
c
[412203−32−5]
d
[41−10−36−35−5]
e
[4−10063−302]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a real 3×3 matrix that has one real eigenvalue λ1 with corresponding eigenvector v1, and two complex eigenvalues λ2=λ―3 with corresponding eigenvectors v2=v―3, then A=PBP−1, where B=[λ1000Re(λ2)Im(λ2)0−Im(λ2)Re(λ2)],P=[|||v1Re(v2)Im(v2)|||]. Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

From our block diagonal matrix B=[7000480−84], we deduce that the first column of P will correspond to the real eigenvector v1 and the second and third columns of P will correspond to the complex eigenvector v2:

P=[41−10−63−30−5]

content.knowledge_point: Calculating the Invertible Matrix in Block Diagonal Form of a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ represents a rotation-scaling matrix:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} \\ -6+3\text{i} \\ -5\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 8 \\ 0 & -8 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=7$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=4+8\text{i},$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 8 \\ 0 & -8 & 4\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first column of $P$ will correspond to the real eigenvector ${v}_{1}$ and the second and third columns of $P$ will correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{2}:$

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & -6 & 3 \\ -3 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}]
$$

Question 14
?

Consider the vectors v1 and v3 and the block diagonal matrix B shown below, where the 2×2 block of B represents a rotation-scaling matrix: v1=[5+7i1+ii],v3=[10−2],B=[−1−202−1000−2] The vectors v1 and v3 are the eigenvectors of a matrix A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1=−1−2i and λ3=−2, respectively. Given that A=PBP−1, which of the following could be the matrix P?

a
[5171010−21]
b
[57111001−2]
c
[75111010−2]
d
[157011−201]
e
[175011−211]
Submit

decision.explanation: The block for −1−2i comes first, so choose P=[Re(v₁),Im(v₁),v₃]. Its columns are (5,1,0)^T, (7,1,1)^T, and (1,0,−2)^T, exactly option b. Its determinant is 5, so it is invertible, and B(1,i,0)^T=(−1−2i)(1,i,0)^T verifies the pairing.

after.name: Question 14
after.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ represents a rotation-scaling matrix:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}5+7\text{i} \\ 1+\text{i} \\ \text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-1-2\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=-2,$  respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{3},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{2}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{1}={\overset{―}{v}}_{2},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 \\ -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {\lambda }_{3}\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ \text{Re}({v}_{1}) & \text{Im}({v}_{1}) & {v}_{3} \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ will correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the third column of $P$ will correspond to the real eigenvector ${v}_{3}:$

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}5 & 7 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a real 3×3 matrix that has one real eigenvalue λ3 with corresponding eigenvector v3, and two complex eigenvalues λ1=λ―2 with corresponding eigenvectors v1=v―2, then A=PBP−1, where B=[Re(λ1)Im(λ1)0−Im(λ1)Re(λ1)000λ3],P=[|||Re(v1)Im(v1)v3|||]. content.knowledge_point: Calculating the Invertible Matrix in Block Diagonal Form of a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ represents a rotation-scaling matrix:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}5+7\text{i} \\ 1+\text{i} \\ \text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-1-2\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=-2,$  respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{3},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{2}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{1}={\overset{―}{v}}_{2},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 \\ -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {\lambda }_{3}\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ \text{Re}({v}_{1}) & \text{Im}({v}_{1}) & {v}_{3} \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ will correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the third column of $P$ will correspond to the real eigenvector ${v}_{3}:$

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}5 & 7 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=4+6\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=-1,$  respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$

Question 15
?

Consider the vectors v1 and v3 and the block diagonal matrix B shown below, where the 2×2 block of B represents a rotation-scaling matrix: v1=[4−i−5i3−2i],v3=[1−34],B=[460−64000−1] The vectors v1 and v3 are the eigenvectors of a matrix A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1=4+6i and λ3=−1, respectively. Given that A=PBP−1, which of the following could be the matrix P?

a
[4−110−54−2−20]
b
[4−100−2−3350]
c
[5−11−2−5−31−20]
d
[4−110−5−33−24]
e
[4−113−5−3301]
Submit

decision.explanation: Choose P=[Re(v₁),Im(v₁),v₃], matching the order and signs of B. The columns are (4,0,3)^T, (−1,−5,−2)^T, and (1,−3,4)^T, giving option d. Its determinant is −80, so it is invertible; P(1,i,0)^T=v₁ verifies the pairing with 4+6i.

after.name: Question 15
after.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ represents a rotation-scaling matrix:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}4-\text{i} \\ -5\text{i} \\ 3-2\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}4 & 6 & 0 \\ -6 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=4+6\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=-1,$  respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{3},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{2}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{1}={\overset{―}{v}}_{2},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 \\ -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {\lambda }_{3}\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ \text{Re}({v}_{1}) & \text{Im}({v}_{1}) & {v}_{3} \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}4 & 6 & 0 \\ -6 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ will correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the third column of $P$ will correspond to the real eigenvector ${v}_{3}:$

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & -3 \\ 3 & -2 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Question 15

Consider the vectors v1 and v3 and the block diagonal matrix B shown below, where the 2×2 block of B represents a rotation-scaling matrix: v1=[4−i−5i3−2i],v3=[1−34],B=[460−64000−1] The vectors v1 and v3 are the eigenvectors of a matrix A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1=4+6i and λ3=−1, respectively. Given that A=PBP−1, which of the following could be the matrix P?

a
[4−110−54−2−20]
b
[4−100−2−3350]
c
[5−11−2−5−31−20]
d
[4−110−5−33−24]
e
[4−113−5−3301]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a real 3×3 matrix that has one real eigenvalue λ3 with corresponding eigenvector v3, and two complex eigenvalues λ1=λ―2 with corresponding eigenvectors v1=v―2, then A=PBP−1, where B=[Re(λ1)Im(λ1)0−Im(λ1)Re(λ1)000λ3],P=[|||Re(v1)Im(v1)v3|||]. Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

From our block diagonal matrix B=[460−64000−1], we deduce that the first and second columns of P will correspond to the complex eigenvector v1, and the third column of P will correspond to the real eigenvector v3:

P=[4−110−5−33−24]

content.knowledge_point: Calculating the Invertible Matrix in Block Diagonal Form of a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ represents a rotation-scaling matrix:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}4-\text{i} \\ -5\text{i} \\ 3-2\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}4 & 6 & 0 \\ -6 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=4+6\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=-1,$  respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{3},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{2}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{1}={\overset{―}{v}}_{2},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 \\ -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {\lambda }_{3}\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ \text{Re}({v}_{1}) & \text{Im}({v}_{1}) & {v}_{3} \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}4 & 6 & 0 \\ -6 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ will correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the third column of $P$ will correspond to the real eigenvector ${v}_{3}:$

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & -3 \\ 3 & -2 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-5+\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=-3\text{i},$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$

Question 16
?

Consider the vectors v1 and v3 and the block diagonal matrix B shown below, where both 2×2 blocks of B represent rotation-scaling matrices: v1=[−3+i5−2i2+4i3−4i],v3=[24−7i1−2i3+i],B=[−5100−1−500000−30030] The vectors v1 and v3 are the eigenvectors of a matrix A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1=−5+i and λ3=−3i, respectively. Given that A=PBP−1, which of the following could be the matrix P?

a
[5−2−7424−21−31023−413]
b
[1−320−254−7421−2−4331]
c
[5−24−7−31203−431241−2]
d
[−31203−431241−25−24−7]
e
[−31205−24−7241−23−431]
Submit

decision.explanation: Choose P=[Re(v₁),Im(v₁),Re(v₃),Im(v₃)], matching both blocks of B and their imaginary-part signs. This gives option e. The columns are independent because the corresponding complex eigenvectors and their conjugates have four distinct eigenvalues, so P is invertible.

after.name: Question 16
after.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where both $2\times 2$ blocks of $B$ represent rotation-scaling matrices:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-3+\text{i} \\ 5-2\text{i} \\ 2+4\text{i} \\ 3-4\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4-7\text{i} \\ 1-2\text{i} \\ 3+\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & -5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-5+\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=-3\text{i},$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $4\times 4$ real matrix that has complex eigenvalues 

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{2}\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{3}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{4}$ 

with corresponding eigenvectors 

$\,$ ${v}_{1}={\overset{―}{v}}_{2}\,$ and $\,{v}_{3}={\overset{―}{v}}_{4},$ 

then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 & 0 \\ -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{3}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{3}) \\ 0 & 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{3}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{3})\end{aligned}]
$$

and

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ \text{Re}({v}_{1}) & \text{Im}({v}_{1}) & \text{Re}({v}_{3}) & \text{Im}({v}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & -5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the third and forth columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{3}.$ Therefore,

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 5 & -2 & 4 & -7 \\ 2 & 4 & 1 & -2 \\ 3 & -4 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
